result.title: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
result.summary: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is paired with a caption that changes or distorts its narrative. Because the image itself may contain no visible signs of manipulation, methods designed to detect pixel-level artifacts can miss these misleading image-caption pairs. We study this problem using DGM4+, a dataset designed to evaluate the detection of global scene and semantic inconsistencies. We propose a multimodal model that combines image-text representations from SigLIP with visual scene features from DINOv2 through a projection MLP, and adapts Qwen2-VL-7B using LoRA. The model jointly predicts whether an image-caption pair is authentic, identifies the manipulation type, and grounds the misleading caption tokens. On the DGM4+ validation split, the model achieves an F1 score of $0.9679$ for binary authenticity classification. These results suggest that parameter-efficient adaptation of vision-language models is promising for detecting semantic inconsistencies, while also motivating further work on precise token-level grounding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MiD-VLM：将 SigLIP 的图文表示与 DINOv2 的视觉场景特征经投影 MLP 融合，并 LoRA 适配 Qwen2-VL-7B，在 DGM4+ 上同时判别图文对真实性、识别操纵类型并定位误导性 caption token。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究的「全局语义不一致检测与 token 级定位」可作为视觉证据是否被实际使用、能否筛出关键视觉信息的诊断线索供核查；但其为常规融合加 LoRA 微调，未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成或更新。
